NAME: Anatomy and Physiology
DESCRIPTION: Study of the structure and function of the human body, including basic chemistry, biochemistry, and histology. Covers characteristics of life, levels of organization, all major body systems including integumentary, skeletal, muscular, nervous, endocrine, lymphatic, cardiovascular, respiratory, digestive, urinary, and reproductive systems and embryology. Extensive laboratory activities accompany each unit.

NAME: AP Biology (AMST Core)
DESCRIPTION: Elective open to students from all academies. Covers unifying themes in biology: emergent properties, evolution and diversity, form and function, science as a process, and ethical implications. Subject areas: chemistry of life, cellular anatomy and physiology, evolution, classification and diversity, genetics, plant anatomy and physiology, animal anatomy and physiology, ecology. Prepares students for the AP Biology Exam.
PREREQS: Strong background in biology or lab sciences recommended. For AMST Juniors beginning with Class of 2026.

NAME: Biology (AAST Core)
DESCRIPTION: Comprehensive and challenging curriculum supplying a solid scientific foundation. Explores social and ethical issues, critical thinking and problem-solving skills. Weekly laboratory assignments, modeling activities, media and technology, and assigned readings.

NAME: Biology (ACAHA & AVPA Core)
DESCRIPTION: Investigates the composition, diversity, complexity, and interconnectedness of life on Earth. Fundamental concepts of cells, heredity, evolution, and ecology through inquiry-based instruction and laboratory experience. Topics include cell biology, homeostasis, photosynthesis, cellular respiration, cell replication, natural selection, and ecology.

NAME: Biology (AMST Core)
DESCRIPTION: Comprehensive course covering fundamental and current topics in biological sciences. Begins with the nature of science and scientific method, then covers biotechnology discoveries. Topics include study of life, chemistry, biochemistry, cell biology, homeostasis, cellular respiration, and photosynthesis.

NAME: Biology / General Biology (ATCS & ABF Core)
DESCRIPTION: General Biology is a comprehensive course covering fundamental and current topics in the biological sciences. Covers the nature of science, scientific method, biotechnology realm discoveries. Topics include study of life, chemistry, biochemistry, cell biology, homeostasis, cellular respiration, and photosynthesis.

NAME: Biology (AEDT Core)
DESCRIPTION: Comprehensive and challenging curriculum supplying a solid scientific foundation. Explores social and ethical issues, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills. Hands-on exploration through laboratory assignments, modeling activities, media and technology, and assigned readings.

NAME: Experimental Biology
DESCRIPTION: Introduces students to experimental design, basic lab skills, and data collection and analysis. Topics include project development, experimental design, primary literature, bioinformatics, technical writing, laboratory techniques, data collection and analysis, representing data in figures, and conveying technical information. Students spend one trimester with each biology research teacher.

NAME: AP Biology (Elective)
DESCRIPTION: Elective open to students from all academies. Same content as core AP Biology. Covers unifying themes in biology. Prepares students for the AP Biology Exam.
PREREQS: Strong background in biology or lab sciences recommended

NAME: IB Environmental Systems & Societies SL
DESCRIPTION: Systems approach methodology. Aims to promote understanding of environmental processes from local to global scale, provide knowledge and skills for environmental issue analysis, promote critical awareness of cultural perspectives, recognize technology's role in environmental problems, appreciate value of international collaboration, and understand the links between human society and the environment.

NAME: Agricultural Research Methods
DESCRIPTION: Second required course for students to enter the Agriscience Program. Students identify a research topic and prepare their lab notebook to engage in experimental research. Anticipated to enter research project into FFA Agriscience Fair and/or other competitions.

NAME: Applications of Biology in Human Medicine
DESCRIPTION: Surveys the latest trends and discoveries in biosciences shaping modern medicine. Topics include CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing, mRNA vaccine development, cancer immunology, DNA sequencing, personalized medicine, and recombinant DNA technology.

NAME: Agriscience Research
DESCRIPTION: Students use scientific principles and emerging technologies to solve complex AFNR problems. Research takes place in the Environmental Science Center and greenhouse. Projects may involve plants, food, biofuels, marine organisms, and sustainable practices. FFA membership required to participate in NJ State FFA Agriscience Fair.

NAME: Bioethics
DESCRIPTION: Application of ethics to medicine. Multidisciplinary course blending law, philosophy, humanities, and medicine. Addresses significant questions including the ends and purposes of life sciences, healthcare, distributive justice, global healthcare, meaning of life and death, pain and suffering, and rights and responsibilities.

NAME: Botany
DESCRIPTION: Study of plant anatomy and morphology. Introduces students to growth, maintenance, and life cycles of all members of the Plant Kingdom. Special emphasis on flowering plants and their use as food, fuel, and fiber. Laboratory-based course utilizing knowledge of cell anatomy and biochemistry.

NAME: Cell Biology Research
DESCRIPTION: Students conduct independent research in cell and molecular biology. Students develop a research project, design and conduct experiments, collect and analyze data, and present findings at fairs/competitions or publish to a professional journal. Scheduled twice per week on an individual basis.
PREREQS: AMST: 1 trimester of Experimental Biology; All other Academies: Research in Cell Biology elective

NAME: Developmental Biology I
DESCRIPTION: Study of all aspects of growth and differentiation. Introduction to concepts and discoveries in developmental biology including various modes of development from embryonic development to limb regeneration. Embryonic and adult stem cells discussed in detail with respect to regenerative medicine. Also addresses ethical issues with stem cell research.

NAME: Global Climate Change
DESCRIPTION: Explores physical principles involved in planetary scale energy budgets and how changes affect chemical and biological processes on Earth. Students develop understanding of mechanics of climate change and investigate options for mitigation and adaptation.
PREREQS: Knowledge of Biology and Chemistry helpful

NAME: Intro Agriscience
DESCRIPTION: Gateway course for the Agriscience Research program. Introduces students to the science of modern agriculture, including botany, zoology, chemistry, molecular biology, earth science, and engineering practices. Provides fundamentals required to develop plans for a successful research project in agriscience.
PREREQS: One of the prerequisites for Agriscience research

NAME: Introduction to Cancer Biology
DESCRIPTION: Introduces students to the multifaceted field of cancer biology. Covers principles of cancer biology, cellular and molecular mechanisms that regulate cancer, and common detection and treatment strategies. Uses case studies, interactive media, and classroom discussions.

NAME: Introduction to Forensics
DESCRIPTION: Explores physical principles involved in planetary scale energy budgets and how changes to these budgets affect chemical and biological processes on Earth. Students develop a solid understanding of the mechanics of climate change, and investigate options for mitigation and adaptation.

NAME: Introduction to Surgical Techniques
DESCRIPTION: Application required; 24 students (8 per trimester) chosen from applicant pool. Offers Juniors the opportunity to gain research experience in a surgical setting at Englewood Hospital and Medical Center (EHMC). Students learn fundamentals of surgical techniques utilizing an in vivo animal model. Covers surgical preparation, aseptic technique, micro-suturing, bioethics, tissue collection, and post-operative care.
PREREQS: Completed application required; open to 11th grade only

NAME: Introduction to Microscopy
DESCRIPTION: Surveys light and electron microscopy techniques, illustrating how to use imaging tools to answer scientific questions. Provides hands-on access to laser scanning confocal and electron microscopes. Lab-based course.

NAME: Research in Cell Biology
DESCRIPTION: Prerequisite elective required for independent research in cell/molecular biology. Introduces students to primary scientific literature and how to use it to develop a research project proposal. Covers basics of working with cultured cells and molecular analysis techniques. Does not count as a science, biology, or medical elective.

NAME: Sports Medicine
DESCRIPTION: Students learn about the most common sports injuries along with their common treatments. Covers anatomy and physiology of injuries including ACL, MCL, and LCL sprains. Students make a video of a real-life sports injury with appropriate prognosis, treatment, and timetable for return.

NAME: Topics in Oncology
DESCRIPTION: 20+ year Expert Series elective providing experience for students considering healthcare careers. Topics on pediatric oncology and hematology discussed with guest speakers. Students prepare by doing assigned readings, viewing PowerPoints, and preparing questions. Evaluation via student journals written after speaker seminars.

NAME: Business Finance Applications
DESCRIPTION: Introductory course exploring important business financial concepts. Covers financial accounting, financial statement preparation and analysis, US and international financial markets, financial institutions, and corporate financial management. At year-end, students work in teams to create a comprehensive business plan.

NAME: IB Business Management SL
DESCRIPTION: Two-year course using the IB course outline. Year 1: Focus on business functions, management processes, and decision-making in contemporary contexts. Year 2: Covers Marketing and Operations Management, applying business theory and principles to practical business situations.

NAME: IB Economics HL
DESCRIPTION: Two-year course. Year 1: Introduces economics as a social science; covers scarcity, choice, Production Possibilities Frontier, micro-economic theory including markets, supply, demand, equilibrium, price controls, elasticities, theory of the firm, and market failure. Year 2: Focus on Macroeconomics and Global Economy. Revolves around 9 fundamental concepts: Scarcity, Choice, Efficiency, Equity, Economic well-being, Sustainability, Change, Interdependence, and Intervention.

NAME: Financial Literacy Online
DESCRIPTION: Asynchronous, self-paced, online class teaching real-world finance and practical life experience. Students practice managing money, test decision-making skills, and tackle realistic financial dilemmas. Covers credit cards, auto loans, insurance, building and maintaining healthy credit, qualifying for a mortgage, and more.

NAME: Management Marketing
DESCRIPTION: Explores the nature and scope of business including different forms of business ownership, management, internal and external forces, legal environment, ethical decision-making, and marketing methods. Focuses on the movement of goods and services from producers to customers.

NAME: AP Macroeconomics
DESCRIPTION: Covers dynamics of the economy including business cycles, unemployment, inflation, and growth. Topics include basic measures of economic activity, aggregate demand and supply, the Federal Reserve System, monetary and fiscal policy, and international economics including world trade, capital flows, and foreign exchange rates. All students must take AP exam in May.

NAME: AP Microeconomics
DESCRIPTION: Study of individual players in the circular flow of the economy. Covers decision making by individual units, individual markets, specific goods and services, and product and resource prices. Studies how consumers, firms, and government make economic decisions. All students must take AP exam in May.

NAME: Business of Sports
DESCRIPTION: Overview of sports business, a $73 billion dollar industry. Covers revenues and expenses of running a professional sports franchise, fantasy sports, agents, business managers, branding, endorsements, and wagering. Students make a video of a business proposal for a new sports business.

NAME: Federal Reserve Challenge I
DESCRIPTION: Prepares students to compete at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's Fed Challenge. Students research economic issues, write a research paper exploring a specific research question. Tryout process required to be selected for the team.
PREREQS: Only available to ABF academy; tryout process required

NAME: Introduction to Entrepreneurship
DESCRIPTION: Explores the entrepreneurial process and the knowledge, tools, and skills required to be successful entrepreneurs. Focus on identifying and evaluating opportunities for new businesses. Key concepts include industry factors, market and competitive factors, and customer needs. Students work on development of a new business idea.
PREREQS: Not available to ABF & ACAHA academies

NAME: Marketing
DESCRIPTION: Introduction to the study of methods and institutions involved in the movement of goods and services from producers to customers. Emphasis on consumerism, social and legal aspects, market understanding and decision-making, pricing, distribution, promotion, and product policies.
PREREQS: Not available to ABF & ACAHA academies

NAME: Markets and Trading
DESCRIPTION: Introduction to financial markets and the securities traded in those markets. Includes lectures, classroom discussion, and hands-on use of Bloomberg and other trading software. Covers current economic developments and stock and equity options markets. Students keep a Trading Journal and Daily Journal. Final portfolio project required.

NAME: AP Chemistry (AAST Core)
DESCRIPTION: Lab science course covering Equilibrium, Acid/Base Equilibrium, Atomic Structure, Structure and Bonding, Kinetics, Thermodynamics, and Electrochemistry. Also includes spectroscopy and separation technologies, and a dedicated unit on Organic Chemistry beyond the typical AP scope.

NAME: Chemistry (AAST Core)
DESCRIPTION: Covers atomic structure, chemical nomenclature, chemical bonding, stoichiometry, chemical reactions, solution chemistry, introductory acid-base chemistry, and gas behavior. Prepares AAST students for sophomore chemistry. Includes lab rotation every third Wednesday.

NAME: Chemistry (AMST Core)
DESCRIPTION: Covers chemical nomenclature, stoichiometry, types of chemical reactions, thermochemistry, gases, atomic structure, chemical bonding and molecular geometry, liquids, solids and solutions, chemical equilibrium, and acids and bases. Designed to give medical students thorough understanding of chemical compounds. Includes laboratory component.

NAME: Chemistry I (AEDT Core)
DESCRIPTION: Covers atomic structure and understanding and quantifying chemical reactions. Students develop thorough understanding of the structure of atoms, molecules, and compounds and their reactivity. Includes additional laboratory rotation for safe lab practices, recordkeeping, and techniques.

NAME: Chemistry (General Elective)
DESCRIPTION: Covers atomic structure, behavior of gases, thermodynamics, acids and bases, and chemical equilibrium. Includes laboratory component where students keep a laboratory notebook and learn key components of recordkeeping and how to produce a good laboratory report.

NAME: Chemistry II (AEDT Core)
DESCRIPTION: Covers understanding chemical reactions with real life applications, behavior of gases, thermodynamics, chemical equilibria, and acid/base chemistry. Also covers oxidation/reduction reactions, heat exchange, and quantifying equilibria. Includes additional laboratory rotation.

NAME: Chemical Systems & Engineering
DESCRIPTION: Introduces students to chemical concepts with connections to chemical engineering. Topics include Thermodynamics, Atomic Structure, Bonding, Solutions and States of Matter, Kinetics, Equilibrium, Acid-Base Equilibrium, and Electrochemistry. Labs may include block flow diagrams, desalination, engineering design processes, chemical reaction optimization, and testing physical properties.

NAME: AP Chemistry (Elective)
DESCRIPTION: Systematic review of previous chemistry courses with additional new material. Topics include gas laws, stoichiometry, equilibrium, acid base chemistry, atomic theory, structure and bonding, thermodynamics, chemical reactions, states of matter, colligative properties, kinetics, electrochemistry, and organic chemistry.
PREREQS: Department approval required for other academy students

NAME: Advanced Topics in Chemistry (Full Year)
DESCRIPTION: Expands on concepts found in traditional high school chemistry while introducing foundational and 'leading edge' topics not found in AP science classes. Themes: Materials of Modern Living, The Future of Energy, and 21st Century STEM Trends. Includes demonstrations, hands-on activities, guest speakers, and field trips.
PREREQS: AP Chemistry, AP Biology, AP Physics, or instructor approval

NAME: Advanced Topics in Chemistry (Trimester)
DESCRIPTION: Explores historically significant advances in chemistry not covered in previous science classes. Focus on important advances from the past decade likely to be active research areas as BCA students enter these fields.
PREREQS: Completed at least two (2) trimesters of AP Chemistry

NAME: Chemistry Research
DESCRIPTION: Project-based elective for independent student research in the emerging field of chemistry and nanotechnology. Students perform their own experiments, collect data using state-of-the-art scientific equipment, and present outcomes through various science competitions.

NAME: Forensic Science
DESCRIPTION: Covers basic principles of Forensic Science. Students learn to identify, examine, and collect evidence such as fingerprints, hair and fiber samples, and blood spatter. Lab-based elective. Culminates with the 'Crime Scene in a Box' project.

NAME: Foundations of Nano
DESCRIPTION: Prerequisite for chemistry/nanotechnology independent research. Students explore fundamental theories and experimental practices of nanoscience and nanotechnology with focus on chemical, biological, and electronic applications. Includes invention challenge project presentation, lab worksheet, and take-home test.

NAME: Medicinal Chemistry
DESCRIPTION: Introductory overview to the field of medicinal chemistry. Explores how the structure of bioactive medicinal compounds impacts how they behave in the body. Topics include drug design to bind to a specific receptor, drug formulation for immediate or gradual release, and treatment of drug overdose.
PREREQS: Must have already completed 1 chemistry class

NAME: Organic Chemistry I
DESCRIPTION: Focuses on learning and understanding the basic principles of organic molecule structures and organic reaction mechanisms. Designed as an understanding-based approach rather than rote memorization.
PREREQS: Completion of at least two (2) trimesters of a sophomore core chemistry class, or enrollment with instructor approval

NAME: Organic Chemistry II
DESCRIPTION: Continues discussions regarding the structure and reactivity of commonly encountered classes of organic molecules. Discussion-based, no lab component. Topics include stereochemistry, substitution reactions, elimination reactions, chemistry of alkenes, alkynes, aldehydes, and ketones.

NAME: Strategies in Chemistry
DESCRIPTION: Provides students with additional support for their core chemistry class. Most useful to students taking a freshman or sophomore core chemistry class wishing to get extra help on problem-solving skills and essential chemistry concepts.

NAME: Advanced Topics in Computer Science Sequence
DESCRIPTION: Three-trimester sequence: (1) Math Foundations of Computer Science – Boolean Algebra, inductive techniques, set theory, cardinality of infinite sets; (2) Functional Programming – functional programming paradigm, immutability, recursion, lambdas, lambda calculus; (3) Computational Theory – finite state machines, pushdown automata, Turing machines, Church-Turing thesis. Culminates in building a full interpreter for Lambda Calculus.

NAME: AP Computer Science A / Data Structure
DESCRIPTION: Based on College Board syllabus plus additional data structures topics. Covers program design and implementation, algorithm analysis, object-oriented programming, queues, stacks, linked lists, heaps, and binary trees. Emphasizes programming methodology with focus on problem solving and algorithm development.

NAME: Capstone Computer Science
DESCRIPTION: Provides real-world experience of developing a large project for a client with a small team. Students are introduced to Agile-style project management and learn new technologies and techniques as needed.

NAME: Introduction to Computer Science
DESCRIPTION: Introduces students to computer science and programming. Begins with Python, then moves to web programming with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Two open-ended group projects are built to promote team-based development skills.

NAME: AP Computer Science A (Elective)
DESCRIPTION: Covers core aspects of computer science for creating solutions that are understandable, adaptable, and reusable. Includes development and analysis of algorithms and fundamental data structures, use of logic and formal methods.
PREREQS: Foundations of Computer Science (1, 2, and 3) OR Instructor Approval

NAME: Foundations of Computer Science (Full Year)
DESCRIPTION: Introduction to concepts and practices of computer programming with emphasis on program flow and structure. Instruction in Java though concepts are universal across programming languages. Upon completion, students will be prepared to enroll in AP Computer Science A.

NAME: IB Computer Science SL
DESCRIPTION: Requires understanding of fundamental concepts of computational thinking and knowledge of how computers and digital devices operate. Students study how computer science interacts with and influences cultures and society. Students develop computational solutions.
PREREQS: Foundations of Computer Science (1, 2, and 3) AND Structured Query Language OR Instructor Permission

NAME: Introduction Systems Programming
DESCRIPTION: Students move beyond abstractions of modern programming languages. Covers assembly language (6502 chipset), instruction processing, byte-level memory architecture, bash shell in Linux, C programming, pointers, data structures (array lists, linked lists, stacks), computer networks, network programming, and threading.
PREREQS: Foundations of Computer Science (non-ATCS) OR Intro to Computer Science (ATCS) OR Instructor Permission

NAME: Software Engineering
DESCRIPTION: Explores how very large projects can be engineered to succeed as they scale. Focus on test-driven development and programming design patterns. Course takes place within Unity and C#.

NAME: Web Apps with Databases
DESCRIPTION: Introduction to developing web applications. Students strengthen skills in HTML, CSS, and browser-based JS, learn to query and update data in an existing MySQL database, design and implement new relational databases, and build a full data-enabled web application.
PREREQS: Foundations of Computer Science (non-ATCS) or Intro to Computer Science (ATCS)

NAME: Artificial Intelligence
DESCRIPTION: Intensive introduction to the broad field of AI. Covers computational representations of knowledge and reasoning. Topics include uninformed and informed search, adversarial search, and reinforcement learning, with applications including route planning and game playing.

NAME: Assembly Language Basics
DESCRIPTION: Students learn how the computer understands and executes programs. Covers basics of assembly language (6502 chipset), fundamental concepts of instruction processing, and byte-level memory architecture.
PREREQS: Intro to Computer Science (ATCS) OR Foundations of Computer Science (non-ATCS)

NAME: Computer Security
DESCRIPTION: Provides students with basic knowledge required to be involved in the field of computer security. Covers how computers work at very low levels, how attacks are made in the digital sphere, and foundations for digital defense.
PREREQS: Intro to C Programming or permission of instructor

NAME: Foundations of Computer Science (Trimester)
DESCRIPTION: Trimester 1: Introduction to Java – input/output, conditionals, loops, methods. Trimester 2: Object-oriented programming – objects, behaviors, properties, inheritance. Trimester 3: ArrayLists and arrays to store sequences of data and standard array/list patterns.
PREREQS: Trimester 2: Foundations of CS 1 or Instructor Permission; Trimester 3: Foundations of CS 2 or Instructor Permission

NAME: Front End Web Dev
DESCRIPTION: Students learn to create basic webpages using HTML and CSS, then advance to animation, UX/UI design patterns, responsive design, more in-depth CSS, JavaScript, and standard JavaScript libraries.
PREREQS: Foundations of Computer Science-2 (non-ATCS) or ATCS may take beginning 2nd trimester of 9th grade

NAME: Intro Web App Development
DESCRIPTION: Students design, build, and deploy their first web applications, exploring available web technologies and their advantages and disadvantages.
PREREQS: All students: Structured Query Language; Additionally for non-ATCS students: Foundations of Computer Science-2

NAME: Machine Learning
DESCRIPTION: Introduction to the discipline of machine learning and a survey of popular supervised learning techniques. Covers algorithms and statistical models to make decisions without explicit programming, relying on patterns and inferences found in data.
PREREQS: Foundations of Computer Science (non-ATCS) or Intro to Computer Science (ATCS)

NAME: Processors
DESCRIPTION: Two-course sequence. Part 1 focuses on combinational logic using AND, OR, XOR, and NOT. Culminates with creation of a virtual version of the 1970s retro digital game 'Lights Out'.
PREREQS: Co-requisite: AP Computer Science, Systems Programming, or Assembly Language Basics

NAME: Processors II
DESCRIPTION: Part Two of the processors sequence. Focuses on processor architecture, culminating in the creation of your very own processor.

NAME: Sockets and Threading
DESCRIPTION: Introduces threading and sockets. Threading enables multiple simultaneous execution points to increase program speed. Sockets allow communication between computer programs on different computers for network-based applications like chat servers or online games. Taught in Java.
PREREQS: Prerequisite or Co-requisite: AP Computer Science A

NAME: Structured Query Language
DESCRIPTION: Students learn to design, update, and query relational databases using SQL.
PREREQS: ATCS students may take beginning 2nd trimester of 9th grade; Other academies: may be taken with or after Foundations of Computer Science-2

NAME: Culinary Design (Semester)
DESCRIPTION: Introduction to the art of cooking. Students learn about savory and sweet dishes while practicing safe food habits and maintaining a safe working environment. Topics include knife handling, basic cooking skills, safety and sanitation, weighing and measuring ingredients, and different mixing methods in baking.

NAME: Entrepreneurship & Advanced Culinary Arts
DESCRIPTION: Builds on previous fundamental skills from 9th and 10th grade courses. Enhances the field of study of hospitality industry: food & beverage and lodging. Builds culinary theory principles to mastery. Online ServSafe class administered.

NAME: Hospitality Management
DESCRIPTION: Presents basics of operational theory of hospitality management and culinary arts under the functions of planning, organizing, staffing, and controlling. Administered through the National Restaurant Educational Foundation's ProStart Management Curriculum. Covers entrepreneurship and management.

NAME: Hotel Management & Culinary Theory
DESCRIPTION: Builds on fundamental skills from 9th grade courses. Enhances the field of study of hospitality industry: food & beverage and lodging. Builds on culinary theory principles. Focuses on development of flexible skills essential for success in a Hospitality career.

NAME: Introduction Hospitality Culinary Arts
DESCRIPTION: Overview of the many dimensions of the hospitality industry. Explores food, beverage and lodging segments, historical foundations, and career possibilities. Students receive exposure to fundamentals of Culinary Arts including safety, sanitation, knife skills, soup, and sauce preparation.

NAME: Culinary Design (Trimester Elective)
DESCRIPTION: Four specialty tracks: Baking for the Holidays, Classical French Cuisine, All About Chocolate, and World Cuisine. Each explores different culinary techniques and ingredients.

NAME: ProStart Competition
DESCRIPTION: Students demonstrate knowledge of the restaurant and hospitality industry by developing a new restaurant concept including descriptions, menu, floor plan, interior/exterior design, SWOT analysis, organizational chart, recipes/costing, and marketing tactics.

NAME: Advanced Electrical Engineering
DESCRIPTION: Builds on the intermediate electrical engineering course. Expands use of operational amplifiers for interfacing sensors and designing active filters. Covers microcontrollers for embedded control, Electronic Design Automation, schematic entry, circuit board layout, and generating Gerber files.

NAME: Computer Assisted Design
DESCRIPTION: Introduction to Engineering Design I (IEDI). Three-trimester course covering webpage-based HTML codes, 2D and 3D computer aided design (CAD), and oral and written presentation. Students learn Autodesk Inventor software, 3D Studio Max software, and visualization tools of CAD.

NAME: Electronics
DESCRIPTION: Introduction to fundamentals of electronics and circuit prototyping. Covers diodes, capacitors, resistors, transistors, op-amps, TIP120 and IC-555 timers. Students apply concepts through labs and trimester projects. Covers bread-boarding, PCB fabrication, and use of test instruments.

NAME: Engineering Applications Programming
DESCRIPTION: Focuses on engineering analysis using MatLab and Fusion 360. MatLab used for modeling engineering problems for analysis, simulation, and data presentation. Fusion 360 used for FEA (Finite Element Analysis) for stress, deflection, and thermal simulations. Applications include mechanical, dynamic, thermal, electrical, and financial problems.

NAME: Engineering Capstone
DESCRIPTION: Builds on skills from IED, POE, Electronics, CIM, and traditional academic coursework. Supports a project in student's preferred area of engineering. Includes fabrication of student inventions, architectural designs, or engineering competitions. Culminates with a working prototype and product presentation.

NAME: Electrical Engineering
DESCRIPTION: Covers basic concepts in electrical engineering: relationships between Voltage, Current, Impedance and Power; passive components; active components (diodes and transistors); PN junction; operational amplifiers; embedded control using microcontrollers. Includes many lab exercises.

NAME: Introduction to Object Oriented Programming
DESCRIPTION: Introduces students to the Python programming language. Focus on developing algorithms and simulations of physical systems. Covers variables, operators, branches, loops, lists, functions, classes, user input, and output formatting. Students write code for plotting, line-fitting, numerical integration, and simulation.

NAME: Makerspace
DESCRIPTION: Introduces students to engineering principles, mechanical drawing, materials, tools, equipment, and machining techniques. Students fabricate various items using metalworking equipment. Skills include using a drill and tap chart, marking out work, center punching, spot drilling, drilling, tapping, countersinking, and deburring.

NAME: Makerspace Program (C Programming)
DESCRIPTION: Introduces students to Arduino C Programming language theory, commands, and architecture. Students learn fundamentals of C programming with Arduino hardware, microcontrollers, and sensors. Students prototype circuits and learn to use simulation software.

NAME: Materials Tolerances
DESCRIPTION: Students learn about materials used in engineering and technology. Covers materials science and technology (MST) including polymers, metals, and concrete. Focus is on student-driven projects with clear, analytical goals using accepted techniques for research.

NAME: BioEngineering
DESCRIPTION: Specialty course in Project Lead the Way pre-engineering curriculum. Focus on biotechnology including biomedical engineering, bio-molecular genetics, bioprocess engineering, and agricultural and environmental engineering. Students engage in engineering design problems related to biomechanics, cardiovascular engineering, genetic engineering, forensics, and bioethics.

NAME: Civil Engineering Architecture
DESCRIPTION: Study of design and construction of residential and commercial building projects. Covers building components and systems, structural design, stormwater management, site design, utilities and services, cost estimation, energy efficiency, and careers in design and construction.

NAME: Design for 3D Printing
DESCRIPTION: Teaches fundamentals of designing items for 3D printing. Students learn Fusion 360 CAD software, DFM (Design for Manufacturing) techniques, and reverse engineering methods. Also covers considerations for future mass production using plastic injection molding.

NAME: Engineering Research
DESCRIPTION: Chance to work on engineering projects in one of the engineering labs. Applied research involving real engineering. Students work with professionals in the field. Access to Electronics lab, Mechanical engineering lab, 3D printers, and Makerspace facilities. Primarily for AEDT students who will be juniors in the fall.
PREREQS: Primarily for AEDT juniors; other academies or rising sophomores with experience will be considered; conversation with engineering teacher required

NAME: Introduction to Robotics
DESCRIPTION: Overview of robot mechanisms, electronic controls, Arduino and Raspberry Pi Microcontrollers, and basic electronics. Topics include motion planning, mechanism design, control design, actuators, sensors, and wireless networking. Weekly labs with Servo, Microcontrollers, Sensors, and Lego NXT.

NAME: Medibotics
DESCRIPTION: Provides information on how to construct and program the LEGO NXT Mindstorms robotic kit, how to build and program for specific simulated medical surgeries, and how to relate these surgeries to STEM areas.

NAME: MRL-Xploration
DESCRIPTION: Introduces students to fundamentals of electronics, microcontrollers, and mechanical design. Serves as a prerequisite for the Mechatronic Research Lab. Students learn to design and prototype circuits, identify electronic components, learn basic Arduino C-Programming, and tool usage and safety procedures.
PREREQS: Serves as prerequisite for Mechatronic Research Lab

NAME: Autodesk Fusion 360
DESCRIPTION: For students with little to no CAD or 3D modeling experience. Introduces essential features of Autodesk Fusion 360. Students learn to draw, sculpt, render, assemble, and animate their own 3D designs, as well as modify already existing 3D models. Not available for AEDT academy.

NAME: American Literature I
DESCRIPTION: Genre-based study that explores American literary history. Covers issues of gender, class oppression, and alienation. Uses novels, plays, essays, short stories, personal narratives, and poetry. Develops listening, speaking, reading, thinking, writing, and researching skills.

NAME: American Literature II
DESCRIPTION: Builds on skills and content from American Literature I. Students become confident critical readers and interpreters. Covers longer works of fiction, poetry, short prose, and nonfiction essays. Focuses on comparing American authors' treatment of major themes coinciding with critical moments in American history.

NAME: IB Literature I & II HL
DESCRIPTION: Two-year course. Year I: Develops skills in literary analysis, survey of literature from various cultures and time periods. Year II: Students study manifestations of literature across cultures. Focuses on understanding factors that contribute to the production and reception of literature.

NAME: IB Literature/Language I & II HL
DESCRIPTION: Two-year course. Year I: Language and literature course exploring the complex and dynamic nature of language, its practical and aesthetic dimensions, and the role language plays in communication. Year II: Students study a wide range of literary and non-literary texts in a variety of media.

NAME: World Literature I & II
DESCRIPTION: Two-year course. Year I: World Literature I Honors – understanding of literary masterpieces from the Ancient World to the Renaissance. Year II: World Literature II Honors – focus on literature from the 16th through 21st centuries. Emphasizes critical analysis, interpretation, and writing skills.

NAME: Creative Writing I & II
DESCRIPTION: Creative Writing I: For students new to creative writing or those who have already begun creative projects. Builds a portfolio of new work. Creative Writing II: For juniors and seniors with existing creative writing projects to revise and refine for submission to contests and writing opportunities.

NAME: Introduction to Dystopian Literature
DESCRIPTION: Students read and analyze literary texts of the 20th and 21st centuries from both America and abroad within the dystopian genre while practicing creative writing skills in the creation of their own dystopian story/stories.

NAME: Introduction to Film Studies
DESCRIPTION: Students are given terms and tools to appreciate and analyze films as works of art and expressions of social context. Examines technique, historical periods, and parts of the world. Students either present an analysis of a chosen film or create a short film.

NAME: Introduction to Journalism / Advanced Journalism Workshop
DESCRIPTION: Introduction: Focuses on journalistic techniques and supports The Academy Chronicle school newspaper. Advanced: Allows students who completed the Intro elective to function as specialists in four areas: section managers and editors, graphic artists, technology managers, and senior staff writers.
PREREQS: Advanced requires completion of Intro elective

NAME: Mythology
DESCRIPTION: Reading and analysis of world mythology to answer: 'Why do so many distinct cultures have similar myths?' Students research parallels among world myths, explore the mythic world of archetype/symbol, study critics who attempt to answer this question, and create an original mythology.

NAME: Nonfiction Writing
DESCRIPTION: Creative nonfiction consisting of true stories, well told. Students read model essays, respond to writing prompts, and practice multiple forms of creative essay writing including the college essay. Students produce at least two creative nonfiction works by end of trimester.

NAME: Playing Shakespeare from Text to Performance
DESCRIPTION: Examines four Shakespearean plays: A Midsummer Night's Dream, As You Like It, Romeo and Juliet, and Macbeth. Focus on helping students overcome the obstacle of Shakespeare's language through performance-based reading.

NAME: Poetry Workshop
DESCRIPTION: Student-driven elective providing the student-poet with the opportunity to explore and refine creative writing skills. Various methods, forms, and techniques practiced in a comfortable workshop atmosphere. Culminates in a poetry reading of selected works.

NAME: Science Fiction as a Literary and Film Genre
DESCRIPTION: Comprehensive, critical analysis of the Science Fiction genre using essays, short stories, and film. Follows a historical timeline from pioneers of Science Fiction (1920s) to contemporary writing. Includes writing, producing, and presenting a trailer for a science fiction movie.

NAME: Songwriters Circle
DESCRIPTION: Examines the connection between history, literature, and music by focusing on specific decades of American life. Students analyze songs and songwriting styles. Students also work on their own compositions performed in a Songwriter's Circle format.
PREREQS: Some proficiency on an instrument preferred but not required

NAME: Stories for Podcasting
DESCRIPTION: Students create their own podcasts that tell personal stories of themselves or others. Listens to samples from NPR's Radio Rookies, This American Life, Freakonomics, and Generation PRX.

NAME: The Personal Essay
DESCRIPTION: Community of trusted feedback for reading and writing about personal subjects. May include college essays, creative nonfiction for other audiences, and multimedia. Students write from prompts and their own interests, share for feedback, and earn grades based on a plan of production rather than solely on the quality of completed work.

NAME: Women in Literature
DESCRIPTION: Pursuit of the study of female characters in contemporary literary works and the women who create them. Begins with Kate Chopin's The Awakening and works by Charlotte Perkins Gilman, Virginia Woolf, Toni Morrison, Alice Walker, Sandra Cisneros, and Amy Tan. Includes an independent study of one female author.

NAME: Theory of Knowledge
DESCRIPTION: Two-year IB course. Explores how knowledge is constructed in varied disciplines. Year 1: Focus on core theme 'knowledge and the knower' plus 3 additional themes (knowledge and language, knowledge and indigenous societies). Year 2: Focus on 2 additional themes (knowledge and technology). Major assessments: 1600-word essay and an exhibition of three original objects.

NAME: IB Research Seminar
DESCRIPTION: One period per week session. Students are introduced to IB Extended Essay. Reviews criteria, peruses sample essays, brainstorms ideas, discovers sources, and writes a research question which is central to the extended essay.

NAME: Advanced Algebra
DESCRIPTION: Covers basic concepts of elementary algebra including Sequences and Linear Functions, Linear Systems, Function Families and Transformation, Working with Functions, Exponential Functions and Logarithms, Quadratics, Higher Degree Functions, Rational Functions, Trigonometry, and Intro to Statistics.

NAME: Advanced Math Analysis I
DESCRIPTION: Begins with logic, then geometry (congruent triangles, quadrilaterals, inequalities, similar polygons, right triangles including trigonometry, circles, constructions, area and volume). Concludes with pre-calculus topics: linear, quadratic, polynomial, exponential, and logarithmic functions, and conic sections. First course in two-course precalculus series.

NAME: Advanced Math Analysis II
DESCRIPTION: Pre-calculus Honors. Designed to prepare students for AP Calculus AB or BC. Covers analysis of polynomial, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions. Topics include sequences, series, polar equations, parametric equations, combinatorics, probability, limits, continuity, and derivatives.

NAME: Advanced Math Topics
DESCRIPTION: Lays foundation for further serious mathematics and physics. Covers linear algebra, vector spaces, linear transformations, Fourier series and analysis, scalar fields, vector fields, directional derivatives, partial derivatives, total derivative, line integrals, and classical partial differential equations.

NAME: Advanced Pre Calculus Discrete
DESCRIPTION: Higher version of Advanced Analysis II. Covers field and set proofs, induction, limits of sequences, trigonometry and complex numbers, linear algebra and calculus through applications of derivatives. More rigorous definitions and sophisticated proofs than AAII.

NAME: AP Analyt Calculus (BC+)
DESCRIPTION: Highly theoretical version of calculus covering all basic material from AP Calculus BC with additional topics. Entirely proof-based. Begins with axiomatizing the real numbers, then covers integrability, limits and continuity, differentiability and applications, methods of integration, sequences and series, and Taylor series.

NAME: AP Calculus AB
DESCRIPTION: Introduction to single variable calculus and preparation for the AP Calculus AB examination. Topics include limits, derivatives, and integrals. Covers finding tangent lines, area of regions, volumes of solids, maximums and minimums, position/velocity/acceleration.

NAME: AP Calculus BC
DESCRIPTION: Corresponds to the AP Calculus BC syllabus. Full-year rigorous introduction to fundamentals of differential and integral calculus with precisely formulated definitions and problem-solving skills. Students are thoroughly prepared to take the BC Advanced Placement Exam.

NAME: AP Statistics
DESCRIPTION: Introductory college-level statistics course. Topics include variation and distribution, patterns and uncertainty, and data-based predictions, decisions, and conclusions. Uses technology, investigations, problem solving, and writing.

NAME: Calculus I
DESCRIPTION: Based on four major concepts: limit, derivative, definite integral, and indefinite integral. Algebraic methods for differentiating and integrating the elementary transcendental functions including trigonometric, logarithmic, and exponential.

NAME: IB Math HL
DESCRIPTION: Two-year curriculum by the IBO. Main topics: statistics, probability, vectors, complex numbers, proofs, binomial theorem extension, Maclaurin series, and differential equations. Students complete a mathematical exploration (essay). Requires thorough knowledge of all math topics learned throughout four years at BCA.
PREREQS: Teacher recommendation; thorough knowledge of all math from BCA; calculus course counts as first year

NAME: IB Math SL
DESCRIPTION: Broad range of topics for students anticipating future studies in chemistry, economics, psychology, and business. Curriculum: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics & probability, and calculus. Senior year focuses on modeling data, statistics, probability, and math exploration.
PREREQS: Calculus I or higher Calculus course

NAME: Linear Algebra & Differential Equations
DESCRIPTION: Introduction to college level Linear Algebra including linear combinations, vector spaces, linear transformations, and eigenspaces. Extends Calculus topics to solve key varieties of differential equations. Culminates in analysis of systems of differential equations including coupled linear systems and nonlinear systems. Major project required.
PREREQS: Calculus AB or BC, or teacher recommendation

NAME: Math Analysis I
DESCRIPTION: Begins with review of Algebra topics, then moves through Algebra II and Precalculus including functions (linear, quadratic, polynomial, exponential, logarithmic, trigonometric). Introduces fundamental Statistics topics and key Geometry concepts.

NAME: Math Analysis II
DESCRIPTION: Comprehensive coverage providing solid preparation for college level courses in calculus, linear algebra, finite mathematical structures, and probability and statistics. Balance of theory and application through theorems, proofs, examples, and solutions.
PREREQS: Placement test, or by teacher recommendation

NAME: Math Structures Proofs
DESCRIPTION: Begins with mathematical and symbolic logic, then a thorough axiomatic introduction to geometry (lines, angles, circles, triangles, larger polygons, non-Euclidean geometries). Introduces trigonometry, then covers algebra topics (quadratic functions, polynomials, conics, exponential and logarithmic functions). Concludes with number theory basics.

NAME: Multivariable Calculus
DESCRIPTION: Equivalent to a typical third semester calculus course in a university sequence. Covers single-variable calculus concepts applied to vector and parametric functions, multi-variable calculus, and vector calculus. Emphasis on practical applications to science and engineering. Students introduced to technical typesetting using LaTeX.

NAME: Statistics
DESCRIPTION: Introduces students to major concepts and tools for collecting, analyzing, and drawing conclusions from data. Four major themes: exploratory analysis, planning a study, probability, and statistical inference. Includes hands-on activities such as M&M's experiments and news broadcasts.

NAME: Data Structures
DESCRIPTION: Comparable to university courses titled 'Algorithms and Data Structures.' Reviews discrete mathematics with big-oh notation. Covers stacks, queues, binary trees, arrays, linked lists, recursion, searching, sorting, binary search trees, hash tables, dynamic programming, graphs, and NP completeness.

NAME: Advanced Math Topics (Trimester)
DESCRIPTION: Miscellaneous advanced topics determined by student and instructor discussion.

NAME: Advanced Pre Calculus Discrete Extension
DESCRIPTION: Continuation of Discrete Mathematics I. Covers pre-calculus type topics (field and set proofs, limits of sequences and series, trigonometry, polar and parametric coordinates, basic limits and derivatives), basic linear algebra, combinatorics, probability and statistics. Includes research/writing projects and introduction to a mathematical word-processing program like TeX. Extension class.

NAME: Analyt Calculus Extension
DESCRIPTION: Highly theoretical version of calculus covering all basic material from AP Calculus BC with additional topics. Entirely proof-based. Extension class.

NAME: BC Calculus Extension
DESCRIPTION: In-depth explanations, discussions, and examples of concepts currently being studied in BC Calculus. Problems that extend the concepts are presented to students. Extension class.

NAME: Cryptology
DESCRIPTION: Study of how to communicate so that only intended partners have access to the communication. Covers historical and modern cryptology, mathematics underlying cryptology, encryption, and decryption techniques used throughout the Internet.
PREREQS: Some background in programming and knowledge of math beyond Freshman level will enable deeper coverage

NAME: Game Theory
DESCRIPTION: Formalized structure for decision making, cost-and-benefit analysis. Covers mathematical games including Nim, Prisoner's Dilemma, Wythoff's Game, Hackenbush, Nash equilibrium, and the game of Domineering.

NAME: Math Problem Seminar
DESCRIPTION: Aimed at Math research and competitions such as Regeneron, YSAP, NRSF, and Google. Students write math contributions in Combinatorics, Number Theory, Geometry, etc. Also prepares for math problem-solving contests such as AMC 10, 12, AIME, USA Math Olympiad, and International Math Olympiad.

NAME: Numerical Analysis
DESCRIPTION: Introduction to techniques in Mathematics and Computer Science used to compute numerical results such as roots of equations, limits, definite integrals, and differential equations. At the intersection of Mathematics and Computer Science.
PREREQS: Intro to Computer Science (ATCS) or Foundations of Computer Science (non-ATCS)

NAME: Skepticism in Data Analysis
DESCRIPTION: Provides powerful tools to cut through intimidating data and misinformation. Topics include Causality, Numbers and Nonsense, Selection Bias, and Data Visualization based on the book 'Calling out BS, the Art of Skepticism in a Data-Driven World.'

NAME: Simulations & Numerical Methods
DESCRIPTION: Explores how to build numerical models for quantitative systems, describe different kinds of models, and use basic computational techniques to run simulations. Students have lessons on formatting mathematics into technical writing syntax. Uses Excel or Google Sheets for numerical modeling.

NAME: Strategies in Mathematics
DESCRIPTION: Provides students with mathematical support based on their individual needs. Appropriate for students in a variety of core classes. Provides opportunities for reflection on inquiry/problem solving and the nature of mathematics.

NAME: Strategy of Card Games
DESCRIPTION: A look at the history and mathematics behind social card games such as Hearts, Euchre, and Cribbage. Students learn the rules and practice playing the games, examine the probabilities involved, and learn basic and intermediate strategies.
PREREQS: Basic understanding of probability and counting, such as covered in Analysis II, recommended

NAME: Advanced Problems in Music Theory & Technology (11th grade core)
DESCRIPTION: Continuation of AP Music Theory in the Digital Age. Covers French, Italian, and German augmented sixth and Neapolitan Chords, composition of fugue expositions, counterpoint including Twentieth-century counterpoint, advanced harmonic analysis including late Romantic literature, analysis of Twentieth-century music, conducting knowledge, performance preparation, and ensemble skills.
PREREQS: At least one year of piano study prior to beginning highly recommended

NAME: AP Music Theory in Digital Age
DESCRIPTION: Prepares students for the College Board AP Exam. Covers fundamentals of tone, intervals, scale and triad construction, phrase analysis and construction, Roman numeral harmonic analysis, non-chord tones, two-voiced species counterpoint, four-part chorale-style composition, dominant and non-dominant seventh chords, analysis of standard repertoire, and analysis of binary and ternary forms. Ear-training comprises nearly 50% of the exam.
PREREQS: At least one year of piano studies highly recommended; exceptions made for instrumentalists with intermediate or better proficiency

NAME: Conducting
DESCRIPTION: Delves into conducting and score-reading. Course is customized to the student's level. Culminates in a rehearsal with one of BCA's major ensembles (band, orchestra, or choir).
PREREQS: Advanced Problems Music Theory & Technology, or teacher's recommendation

NAME: Digital Keyboarding
DESCRIPTION: Open-ended course designed to fit the individual needs of the student. Covers beginner concepts or advanced keyboard harmony (non-traditional clef reading, transposition, harmonization, and fundamentals of improvisation). Students are introduced to the synthesizer and MIDI software.

NAME: Digital Recording Lab (Core)
DESCRIPTION: Students explore various elements of digital recording, audio equipment, and editing. Covers microphones, cables, mixers, amplifiers, wireless systems, and troubleshooting. Recording sessions using GarageBand, Logic Pro, Soundtrap. Projects may include audition material, original songs, formal compositions, arrangements, ringtones, and music videos.

NAME: Electronic Music Synthesis
DESCRIPTION: Applied music course involving fundamentals of MIDI, proceeding through more advanced concepts. Students produce an original composition using Finale software. Course is two trimesters long, taking place in the final two trimesters of senior year.
PREREQS: Mandatory: at least six months of piano studies prior to the course

NAME: Musicianship
DESCRIPTION: Methods course where students learn to play woodwind, brass, string, and percussion instruments. Also covers development of modern instruments and their transposition, conducting techniques, and rhythm dictation. Students conduct in all meters including 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7.
PREREQS: Ability to read music, permission of instructor

NAME: World Music
DESCRIPTION: Arts and humanities course involving the historical development of Western music from its earliest beginnings in Antiquity and Gregorian Chant through the Middle Ages, Renaissance, and Baroque periods.

NAME: Late 20th Century Music
DESCRIPTION: Arts and humanities course involving the historical development of Western music during the Viennese Classical period.

NAME: Post-Romantic Music
DESCRIPTION: Arts and humanities course involving the historical development of Western music beginning in the Romantic period, continuing through Post-Romantic, and culminating in the 20th and 21st centuries.

NAME: Senior Music Media Seminar
DESCRIPTION: Two units: Unit 1 is a 'maker' style course where students construct an authentic musical instrument such as a Telecaster style guitar and mini amplifier. Unit 2: Seniors plan their AVPA-Music Senior Recital (graduation requirement, adjudicated by professional musicians).
PREREQS: Completion of an in-class 'Safety Test' with a score of 100%

NAME: Advanced Problems in Music Theory (12th grade elective)
DESCRIPTION: Continuation of AP Music Theory in the Digital Age. Covers French, Italian, and German augmented sixth and Neapolitan Chords, composition of fugue expositions, counterpoint including Twentieth-century counterpoint, advanced harmonic analysis, conducting knowledge, performance preparation, and ensemble skills.
PREREQS: At least one year of piano study prior to beginning highly recommended

NAME: Concert Band
DESCRIPTION: Large ensemble that performs formal concert music. Includes wind and percussion instruments. Emphasizes performance techniques, general musicianship, and creative/critical thinking. Runs only first and third trimester. Satisfies participation requirement for county, regional, and all-state honors ensembles.

NAME: Concert Choir
DESCRIPTION: Large ensemble of mixed voices. No audition required. Featured in Holiday and Spring Choir & Dance Concerts, performs at school functions, and participates in music festivals.

NAME: Concert Choir (Lunch)
DESCRIPTION: Same choir as the Concert Choir, but at lunchtime. Large ensemble of mixed voices. No audition required. Featured in Holiday and Spring Choir & Dance Concerts, performs at school functions, and participates in music festivals.

NAME: Digital Recording Lab (Elective)
DESCRIPTION: Students explore various elements of digital recording, audio equipment, and editing. Covers microphones, cables, mixers, amplifiers, wireless systems, and troubleshooting. Recording sessions using GarageBand, Logic Pro, Soundtrap.

NAME: Ensemble (Wind & String)
DESCRIPTION: Wind Ensemble: BCA chamber ensembles of 3-8 people including Flute, Clarinet, Saxophone, Mixed Wind, Brass, and Bergen Arts Ensemble. String Ensemble: Piano Trio, String Quartet, etc. Satisfies participation requirement for county, regional, and all-state honors ensembles.

NAME: Guitar I
DESCRIPTION: Comprehensive group lessons covering all facets of guitar performance. Main goal: students with no prior knowledge of guitar/music gain enough skills to begin playing independently. Topics: notation, tablature, chords/notes in first position, ensemble skills. Must have an instrument.

NAME: Guitar II
DESCRIPTION: Comprehensive group lessons taking students through all facets of guitar performance.

NAME: Guitar III
DESCRIPTION: Comprehensive group lessons building on Guitar II. Topics include barre chords, fingerstyle playing, and basic music theory. Students may audition for Guitar & Mandolin Orchestra.

NAME: Guitar & Mandolin Orchestra
DESCRIPTION: Large ensemble performing music on acoustic guitars, bass guitars, mandolins, mandolas, and mandocellos. Satisfies participation requirement for regional and all-state honors ensembles.
PREREQS: Audition required (students who have auditioned for BCA Orchestra on violin, viola, cello, bass may register without audition)

NAME: History of Rock Music
DESCRIPTION: Survey of rock music covering key figures who helped shape rock and roll from its infancy to the 1970s. Includes original song recordings, video clips, documentaries, and class discussions of concurrent events in American history.

NAME: Jazz Band
DESCRIPTION: Medium size combo of about 9-12 musicians. Emphasizes performance techniques, general musicianship, and creative/critical thinking. Satisfies participation requirement for county, regional, and all-state honors ensembles.

NAME: Musicians Workshop
DESCRIPTION: Students build authentic musical instruments or electro-music devices. Covers almost all steps in the 'maker' process from cutting wood to soldering electronics. Team-work skills emphasized. Safe use of materials and tools emphasized. Materials fee required.

NAME: Music & Society
DESCRIPTION: Arts and humanities course involving the historical development of Western music from Antiquity and Gregorian Chant through all stylistic periods: Middle Ages, Renaissance, Baroque (T1), Viennese Classical (T2), and Romantic, Post-Romantic, culminating in the 20th and 21st centuries.

NAME: Orchestra
DESCRIPTION: Large ensemble performing different styles of classical music. Instrumentation includes bowed strings with a limited number of winds/percussion. Runs only first and third trimester. Satisfies participation requirement for regional and all-state honors ensembles.

NAME: Percussion Ensemble
DESCRIPTION: BCA chamber ensemble for accomplished musicians in smaller settings of 3-8 people. Satisfies participation requirement for county, regional, and all-state honors ensembles.

NAME: Pit Orchestra I & II
DESCRIPTION: Performs original Broadway show music for the annual BCA musical. Instrumentation dependent on current show. Runs only second trimester. Satisfies participation requirement for regional and all-state honors ensembles.

NAME: Ukulele Café
DESCRIPTION: Beginner level course for ukulele (soprano and/or concert size instruments). Students learn enough basics to start practicing and performing independently. Culminating experience is a luau-style performance. Students must have their own instrument.
PREREQS: Students must have their own instrument

NAME: Acting I
DESCRIPTION: Students work with physically based techniques and unscripted strategies such as Viewpoints and improvisation to release and open emotional and physical range. Stimulates imagination, puts emphasis on physical actions, and aids in ridding the actor of self-conscious mannerisms.

NAME: Acting II / Playwriting / Theatre History I
DESCRIPTION: Acting, playwriting, and theatre history taught concurrently. Acting: rehearsal process through scene study, ensemble playing, emotional recall, script analysis, and characterization. Playwriting: creating given circumstances, character development, and writing a ten-minute play. Theatre History: Romanticism through contemporary theatre practices.

NAME: Acting III
DESCRIPTION: Develops a close, organic connection between the actor and their technique. Students investigate and utilize their widest possible range. All students prepare 4-6 monologues from contemporary and classical repertory and explore audition technique in preparation for future training or work.

NAME: Acting IV
DESCRIPTION: Advanced scene study class focused on exploration of the text and utilization of technique to determine actor choices for the particular stylistic demands of a text and its period. Scene studies from a variety of major theatrical periods and styles.

NAME: Dance I
DESCRIPTION: Two-trimester course. First component of a four-year dance study. One trimester of ballet and one trimester of musical theatre jazz dance. Covers fundamental positions, techniques, and steps; awareness of body in space; dance terminology and dance history.

NAME: Dance II
DESCRIPTION: Two-trimester course. Consists of both ballet and tap dance. Students practice and advance technical ballet skills and learn ballet history. Second trimester consists of tap dance basics covering musicality, weight change, and tap vocabulary.

NAME: Dance III-IV
DESCRIPTION: Two-trimester course. Students work on artistry, performance technique, audition technique, and connecting with an audience through ballet, tap, and jazz. Explores modern dance, movement improvisation, choreography, and emotional expression. Culminates in a choreography project.

NAME: Directing
DESCRIPTION: Introduces the student to theory and techniques of stage direction. Covers stage visualization, picturization, composition and movement, analysis of scenes, director preparation (casting, rehearsal technique, director/actor relationship), and production values. Culminates in directing a fully staged and produced one-act play.

NAME: Junior Seminar
DESCRIPTION: Students explore theatre, film, and television as a profession and as a business through research, field trips, videoconferences, and guest speakers. Topics include portfolio preparation, resumes, union memberships, agents, job opportunities, auditions, interviews, and advanced training.

NAME: Theatre Fundamentals
DESCRIPTION: Designed to introduce non-AVPA/Theatre students to a general survey of dramatic principles and theatrical conventions. Covers historical perspective, functions of theatre personnel, and practices of the contemporary stage.

NAME: Theatre History I
DESCRIPTION: Beginning with Romanticism and ending with contemporary theatre practices, explores major periods and trends in theatre through examination of performance environments, theatre architecture, design, acting styles, scripts, audiences, and social and cultural conditions of the times.

NAME: Theatre History II
DESCRIPTION: Historical exploration of global theatre arts in relation to developing Eastern and Western world civilizations. Includes study of theatre architecture, styles of acting, development of stage costume, and range of dramatic literature from the Greeks through the closing of the theatre in Great Britain in 1642.

NAME: Voice & Speech I
DESCRIPTION: Develops the actor's vocal range and quality along with training in standard American speech. Uses the Alexander Method and the work of Cicely Berry and Kristin Linklater. Covers vocal range, placement and flexibility with special emphasis on complex and classical texts.

NAME: Voice & Speech II
DESCRIPTION: Continued exercises and technique work. Emphasis on vocal production and placement, breath control, articulation, regionalisms, dialects, and projection. Special emphasis on Voice Over work in the industry with each student creating a voice over demo.
PREREQS: Teacher recommendation and must have participated in at least one production at BCA

NAME: Fashion Design and Sewing
DESCRIPTION: Hands-on ARTS elective where students learn sewing techniques and work with high-end sewing equipment. Includes 'challenge'-style projects similar to Project Runway, creating garments from unusual materials and solving fashion dilemmas.

NAME: Beginner Ballroom
DESCRIPTION: Students work on communication skills by learning to lead and follow in ballroom dance. Ballroom I covers Fox Trot, Rumba, and Swing. Ballroom II covers Tango and Waltz.

NAME: Costume Design
DESCRIPTION: Hands-on, project-based class. Students go through the process of designing costumes for the Senior Directed One Acts. Covers stock at BCA, research the play and period, taking measurements, rendering designs, attending concept production meetings and rehearsals, and working with actors.

NAME: Dance Fundamentals
DESCRIPTION: Learns the secrets of dance training – alignment, musicality, coordination, change of weight in a non-threatening environment. Covers core strength, stretching, isolations, and body alignment. Includes dance moves, turns and leaps across the floor.

NAME: Latin Style of Dance
DESCRIPTION: Students learn different Latin Ballroom dances including salsa, merengue, cha-cha-cha, rumba, bachata, mambo, and the samba. Slower dances focus on strength and style; faster paced dances focus on change of weight, musicality, and change of direction.

NAME: Musical Theater
DESCRIPTION: Student actors undertake the tasks necessary to produce a full-length, fully mounted musical theatre piece. Presentational musical theatre technique in acting, singing, and dance developed with rigorous attention given to ensemble building.

NAME: One Act Play
DESCRIPTION: Hands-on experience in acting techniques, character analysis, proper staging, costuming, prop making, and scenery design through a one-act play. Students audition for roles, memorize and rehearse lines, make costumes, and present the play during an evening play festival. Directors are AVPA: Theatre Seniors.

NAME: Public Speaking
DESCRIPTION: Practice public speaking skills in a fun and supportive environment where everyone improves regardless of starting point.

NAME: Screenwriting
DESCRIPTION: Examines the role of the screenwriter in TV and film. Students study the works of professional screenwriters and investigate different processes of writing for TV, film, and other screen media. Students write their own short screen- or teleplay.

NAME: Stage Management
DESCRIPTION: Students work on the fall play during the elective hour. Learn to work with costumes, props, sets, sound and lights, read drafting, work on the stage, analyze the play, meet with the director and design teams, organize schedules, run technical rehearsals, work with the actors, and develop protocols.

NAME: Stretching and Pilates
DESCRIPTION: Somatic practice (mind-body exercise) developed by Joseph Pilates. Focuses on core strength, flexibility, and alignment. Students gain awareness of their alignment and how negative postures can impact overall health. Once per week class based upon the classic Pilates mat series.

NAME: Theatre Production
DESCRIPTION: Designed to give the student actor an opportunity to develop acting skills, learn character analysis, and participate in the staging, costuming, and scenic design for a full-length play.

NAME: Yoga
DESCRIPTION: Once per week class exploring mindful movement. Focuses on uniting breath with mindful movement, and body with the mind. Covers sun salutations, warriors, twists, balances, backbends, supine poses, and relaxation.

NAME: Yoga Lunch
DESCRIPTION: Yoga class covering a series of postures beginning with gentle spine work and ending with relaxation. Students are exposed to various yoga balances, twists, and inversions. Mats are provided.

NAME: Driver's Education
DESCRIPTION: Prepares students to take the NJ Department of Motor Vehicles written exam. Topics include making effective driving decisions, understanding motor vehicle and traffic laws, learning basic maneuvers, and the safe operation of a vehicle. NJ State DMV written exam administered in class.

NAME: Health - First Aid Online
DESCRIPTION: Family Living curriculum covering four NJ DOE categories: Wellness, Integrated skills (communication, decision making, goal setting, etc.), Drugs and Medicines, and Human Relationships & Sexuality.

NAME: Health & Wellness (9th grade)
DESCRIPTION: Covers topics related to nutritional wellness, sexual health, and current health issues. Covers four NJ DOE categories: Wellness, Nutrition, Drugs and Medicines, and Human Relationships & Sexuality.

NAME: Health & Wellness (11-12 Online)
DESCRIPTION: Two units. Unit 1 (Advanced Topics 1): Knowledge and skills to recognize and handle a medical emergency. Unit 2 (Advanced Topics 2): Explores interpersonal relationships, foundations of human growth and development, responsible personal behavior, and family living. Covers four NJ DOE categories.

NAME: Physical Education
DESCRIPTION: Contributes to the well-being of the student physically, intellectually, emotionally, psychologically, and socially. Emphasis on personal fitness and the pursuit of lifetime activities. Integrates education on the physiology of exercise.

NAME: Advanced Physics
DESCRIPTION: Algebra-based course providing fundamentals of magnetism, wave phenomena, optics, special relativity, and modern physics (quantum, nuclear and particle physics). Emphasizes problem solving and laboratory work.

NAME: AP Physics C (AAST Core)
DESCRIPTION: Calculus-based physics course for college physics/engineering freshmen. Divided into two sections: Mechanics and Electromagnetism. Students may select this to satisfy the 11th grade full year physics requirement. Students must have completed one year of calculus or take Calculus AB/BC concurrently.
PREREQS: One year of calculus before OR Calculus AB/BC concurrently (BC strongly recommended); strong 'A' average in previous physics course

NAME: Physics (AMST Core - 10th grade)
DESCRIPTION: Develops skills and vocabulary for understanding the physical world. Topics of Motion, Forces, Energy, and Momentum. Problem solving techniques primary throughout. Projects, experiments, labs, and problem solving used as major tools.

NAME: Physics (AMST Core - 11th grade)
DESCRIPTION: Covers units on fluids, thermodynamics, electricity, magnetism, waves, and optics. Includes labs on buoyancy, electric current, and lenses and mirrors. All students should be proficient in algebra.

NAME: Physics (ACAHA, ABF, ATCS, AVPA Core)
DESCRIPTION: Covers vectors, kinematics, Newton's Laws of Motion, gravity (and uniform circular motion), energy, momentum, electricity, magnetism, waves, and optics. Labs on friction, electrostatics, and refraction.

NAME: Physics I (AEDT Core)
DESCRIPTION: Covers topics of Motion, Forces, Energy, and Momentum. Students apply problem solving techniques to engineering and physics scenarios. Emphasizes directional properties of Displacement, Velocity, Acceleration, Force, and Momentum.

NAME: Physics II (AEDT Core)
DESCRIPTION: Exposes students to Rotational Motion, Ideal Gas Laws and Kinetic Theory, Heat, Thermal Expansion Thermodynamics, and Electrostatics. Algebra-based course. Emphasizes knowledge of basic laws of nature, application, and experimental and theoretical explanation.

NAME: Advanced Physics for Engineering
DESCRIPTION: Algebra-based course providing fundamentals of magnetism, wave phenomena, optics, special relativity, and modern physics (quantum, nuclear and particle physics). Prepares students to take AP Physics C senior year or enter college engineering programs.
PREREQS: Physics II (AEDT students) or Physics (non-AEDT students)

NAME: AP Physics C (Elective)
DESCRIPTION: Calculus-based physics course for college physics/engineering freshmen. Divided into Mechanics and Electromagnetics. Students must have completed one year of calculus or be enrolled in Calculus AB/BC concurrently.
PREREQS: One year of calculus before OR Calculus AB/BC concurrently (BC strongly recommended); strong 'A' average in previous physics course. If not taken as core physics, may be taken as an elective.

NAME: Astronomy
DESCRIPTION: Study of planets, stars, and the universe. Covers the Copernican Revolution, stellar energy, distance measurements in space, black holes, Einstein's Theory of Relativity, telescopic observation, history of astronomy, Solar System, stars and galaxies, and the search for extrasolar planets. Uses internet resources as a virtual telescope.

NAME: Astrophysics
DESCRIPTION: One-trimester introduction to the physical principles behind celestial phenomena: planetary motion, inner workings of stars, and the nature of the universe. No prior physics course required as all necessary principles are discussed at the start.

NAME: Automotive Dynamics & Engineering
DESCRIPTION: Students study, analyze, and construct solutions to engineering design problems within the automotive industry. Includes deconstruction and analysis of automotive design and function. Students modify, plan, and execute redesigns.

NAME: Einstein's Relativity
DESCRIPTION: One-trimester elective open to all students. Introduces the concepts of both Einstein's theories of special and general relativity. No prior physics course required.

NAME: Earthquake
DESCRIPTION: Explores the awesome realm of the earthquake. Topics include measuring energy released in earthquakes, extent of damage, seismic waves and the structure of the Earth.

NAME: Intro to Volcanology
DESCRIPTION: Broad picture of volcanism. Topics include types of volcanoes, types of lava, causes of volcanoes, detrimental and beneficial effects of volcanoes, and studies of specific volcanic eruptions such as the 79 C.E. eruption that buried Pompeii.

NAME: Math for Physics
DESCRIPTION: Helps students with or anticipating difficulties with Mathematics as applied to problem-solving in Physics. Topics include Geometry, Trigonometry, Advanced Algebra, and (upon request) Calculus.

NAME: Physics Exploration
DESCRIPTION: One-trimester course for students from all Academies. Students explore selected topics in depth with emphasis on related experiments and problem solving skills. Possible topics include classical and quantum mechanics, thermodynamics, electromagnetism, optics, and relativity.

NAME: Physics in Medicine
DESCRIPTION: Open to all students intrigued by medical and physical aspects of bodily functions in living organisms and diagnostics and treatment. Addresses topics not discussed in core Physics classes but included in the MCAT and similar exams.
PREREQS: Previous experience in Physics helpful but not required

NAME: Physics of Music
DESCRIPTION: Explores how principles of physics illuminate the art of music. Topics include waves, sound waves, vibrations in strings, harmonics, resonance in open and closed pipes, frequency patterns in scales (Pythagorean, Just, Equal Tempered Scales), timbres of different instruments, and sound intensity levels in decibels. Knowledge of algebra required.
PREREQS: Knowledge of algebra required; knowledge of music helpful

NAME: Quantum Mechanics
DESCRIPTION: Math-based introduction to Quantum Physics. Topics include wave functions, measurements, quantum states, solutions of Schrödinger's equation, linear algebra and complex numbers, and abstract framework for quantum theory applications. Prior knowledge of differentiation and integrals necessary.
PREREQS: Prior knowledge of differentiation and integrals necessary

NAME: Quantum Physics
DESCRIPTION: Conceptual introduction to Quantum Physics. No prior knowledge required. Topics include early experiments (Blackbody Radiation, Photoelectric effect), wave-particle duality, quantum states and operators, entanglement, double-slit experiment, and uncertainty principle. Serves as preparation for 'Quantum Mechanics' elective.

NAME: Science Olympiad: Get Ready
DESCRIPTION: For students interested in the Science Olympiad contest. Students work on events of their choice, both theoretical and building, alone or in a group. Instructor facilitates students' work and provides guidance.

NAME: Sports Science
DESCRIPTION: Students learn and apply physics and engineering knowledge to understand and enhance interactions within sports and other activities. Students focus on their own extracurricular activities and interests. Projects focus on applying science to understand and enhance performance.

NAME: AP Psychology
DESCRIPTION: Introduces students to the systematic and scientific study of human behavior and mental processes. Topics include biological basis of behavior, sensation and perception, learning and cognition, motivation, developmental psychology, testing individual differences, treatments of psychological disorders, and social psychology.

NAME: IB History of American I & II HL
DESCRIPTION: Two-year course. Year 1: Comparative course integrating history of the Western Hemisphere from colonization through the 20th Century. Year 2: Higher Level IB History continuing from Age of American Expansion through the Great Depression, then 20th century world history (Communism in Crisis, Causes/practices/effects of wars, Cold War). Includes IB Historical Investigation.

NAME: IB 20th Century SL
DESCRIPTION: One-year course. 20th Century World History Course based on a comparative, multi-perspective approach. Focuses on change, causation, and significance. Involves study of political, economic, social, and cultural history, encouraging students to think historically and develop historical skills.

NAME: 20th Century American History I
