DESCRIPTION: For Juniors not in the IB HL program. Beginning with Reconstruction through the dawn of the 21st Century. Develops critical thinking skills for understanding the complexities of social sciences. Includes a yearlong research project focusing on an aspect of American History.

NAME: 20th Century American History II
DESCRIPTION: Honors level continuation of the Global History sequence. Beginning with post-Civil War Reconstruction through the Cold War. Covers political, economic, and social history of the United States through a global lens. Students engage extensively with primary and secondary sources.

NAME: World History I
DESCRIPTION: Covers world history between the Postclassical Era and the revolutions in France, Latin America, and the United States in the early 1800s. Develops history-oriented vocabulary, understanding of political/social/economic systems. Prepares students for the IB history program at BCA.

NAME: World History II
DESCRIPTION: Core Social Studies course. Covers world history from the Rise of Europe in the Renaissance through the French and Haitian Revolutions, the Industrial Revolution, and Imperialism. Pays attention to Europe, China and Far East, India, the Islamic world, Latin America, and Africa.

NAME: American History on Trial
DESCRIPTION: Students explore controversial actions and patterns of behavior of American presidents starting with Thomas Jefferson. Students craft trial cases, investigate and impersonate key historical figures, build understanding of the American judicial process, and collaboratively design a trial packet.

NAME: Contemporary Ethics
DESCRIPTION: Seminar format course on ethics (morality, what is right or wrong in human behavior). Also covers epistemology and metaphysics as connected to ethics. Graded discussions and papers.

NAME: In the Era of Mao
DESCRIPTION: Explores the complex dynamics of Mao Zedong's personality and his continual reinterpretation of Chinese socialism. Investigates the rise of Mao to power, the establishment of the People's Republic of China, The Great Leap Forward, the Great Proletarian Cultural Revolution, and contemporary China's understanding of the era of Mao.

NAME: Model UN
DESCRIPTION: Instructs students in the current state of world affairs and how to argue and debate these issues using Model UN. Students research the United Nations, other international bodies, and international issues, then debate using standard Model UN debate format.

NAME: Modern Russian History I
DESCRIPTION: First of three electives focusing on Russia's history. Covers from the Crimean War (1853-1856) to the Soviet Union on the eve of World War II (1941-1945). Themes: war as a catalyst for political reform, Russia's relations with the West, WWI's impact, inevitability of the Bolshevik Revolution, and challenges facing the new Soviet Government.

NAME: Modern Russian History II
DESCRIPTION: Covers the period of Soviet history from World War II until the collapse of the USSR in 1991. Focus on Soviet contribution to WWII victory, and the Cold War that emerged between the US and Soviet Union after WWII. Concludes with Gorbachev's reforms and the collapse of the Soviet Union.
PREREQS: Modern Russian History I, or teacher recommendation (seniors only)

NAME: Modern Russian History III
DESCRIPTION: Final installment of Modern Russian History electives. Normally covers post-Soviet Russia (1991 to present). Focuses on Cold War, developments leading to Gorbachev's perestroika, the collapse of the Soviet Union, and challenges Russia faced creating a viable political and economic model in the 1990s.
PREREQS: Modern Russian History I & II or teacher recommendation

NAME: Women in East Asia
DESCRIPTION: Explores the concepts of femininity, feminism, and filial piety within the context of China, Korea, and Japan through investigation of primary and secondary sources. Relocates the voice and critical roles women played in pre-20th century East Asia.

NAME: Art Fundamentals
DESCRIPTION: Covers fundamentals in one of the following areas of visual art: video, interactive design, fine arts, or computer imaging. Teacher may accommodate more advanced students through differentiated instruction.

NAME: Design Prod 1
DESCRIPTION: Primary project: C-SPAN Student Cam Competition (5-month documentary video production unit). Other units: introduction to Arduino, Virtual Animals (3D printing), and Cooper Hewitt National High School Design Competition.

NAME: Design Prod 2
DESCRIPTION: Focuses on event management, planning, budgeting, and production. Covers computer-assisted art and design, color theory and psychology, imaging, communication skills, and commercial art business operations.

NAME: Emerging Tech I
DESCRIPTION: Multimedia-themed projects. Advanced topics in web development including animation, UX, UI patterns, responsive design, CSS, JavaScript, and jQuery. Students also learn to develop and prepare designs for laser cutting.

NAME: Emerging Tech II
DESCRIPTION: Project-based units: Cooper Hewitt National High School Design Competition, shooting interviews for 'The Romance Chronicles,' Technology Zoo (animal sculpture from recycled tech elements), Movie Poster/Trailer Production, Creating Animations in Virtual Reality, and Gallery Production.

NAME: Foundation of Visual Art
DESCRIPTION: Introductory foundation course for Visual Art majors. Focus on Elements and Principles of Art/Design and developing student drawing and design skills to a more mature level. Students maintain a sketchbook and portfolio. Students introduced to aesthetics and critique.

NAME: Intro to Visual Art
DESCRIPTION: Introduces students to visual arts and graphic communications. Students create, design, and explore utilizing a wide variety of media and printing processes. Units cover graphic design, computer instruction and production, software usage, fundamental design elements and principles, perspective drawing, digital art, and package design.

NAME: Visual Art Senior Capstone I
DESCRIPTION: Helps students strengthen their art portfolios through development of individual Capstone projects. Supplements with classroom projects enhancing compositional, drawing, painting, and sculpting skills. Capstone projects have the potential to be displayed in a public setting or professionally published.

NAME: Visual Art Senior Capstone II
DESCRIPTION: Students work in a graphic arts facility to acquire advanced skills. Focus on portfolio development and studio projects (personal and group). Students create artwork in traditional media and digitally using Adobe Photoshop and Illustrator. Students create their own books using Adobe InDesign.

NAME: AP Art History
DESCRIPTION: Introductory college-level art history course. Students cultivate their understanding of art history through analyzing works of art and placing them in historical context. Explores culture and cultural interactions, theories and interpretations of art, impact of materials/processes/techniques, and purpose and audience in art historical analysis.

NAME: AP Studio Art
DESCRIPTION: Inquiry-based thinking and making. Students create a portfolio of work demonstrating inquiry through art and design and development of materials, processes, and ideas over the course of a year. Portfolios include works of art, process documentation, and written information. Students submit portfolios in May for evaluation.
PREREQS: Prior experience learning about and making art and design supports success; Pre-AP Studio Art participation prior year is a plus; summer art assignment expected prior to course

NAME: Drawing
DESCRIPTION: Twice a week course focusing on elements of art and principles of design in drawing: composition, proportion, spatial relationships, perspective, volume, light and shadow, value and texture. Students explore traditional and alternative media, drawing styles, techniques, and materials. Satisfies the NJ State requirement for Visual and Performing Arts.

NAME: Design & Digital Media
DESCRIPTION: Students choose an independent project while being exposed to new hardware and software. Disciplines include video production, VR, AR, 3D printing, laser cutting, Arduino, sculpture, animation, Unity game design, interactive installation, and Adobe packages (Photoshop, Illustrator, After Effects).
PREREQS: Must have taken a semester, full-year, or two trimester class with the teacher in order to sign up

NAME: Pre-AP Studio Art
DESCRIPTION: For students who want to build up their art portfolio and consider AP Studio Art for the following year. Course of 2-D art and design and 3-D media exploration. Students can bank works for their AP Studio Art portfolio. Class meets twice per week; students expected to put 2-3 hours per week outside class.
PREREQS: Foundations of Visual Art, or Art Fundamentals courses; Highly recommended for Visual majors

NAME: Visual Art (General)
DESCRIPTION: Non-AVPA students have a chance to experiment with various traditional and digital art techniques to create original works. Projects focus on two-dimensional works, with potential three-dimensional projects if time permits.

NAME: Ceramics
DESCRIPTION: Introductory Ceramics course open to all students. Students explore working with clay using hand-building techniques such as pinch pot, coil, and slab. Fired ceramic objects will be glazed for a completed decorative look.

NAME: Creative Art Workshop
DESCRIPTION: Students explore creative expression through a variety of applied art options including clay hand building, ceramic glazing, 3-D object design, and paper design. Workshop theme changes from trimester to trimester.

NAME: Digital Imaging
DESCRIPTION: Introduction to creating images for Web and Printing using Adobe Photoshop and Illustrator. Units include introduction to software tools and terms, Photoshop projects, Illustrator projects, and animated images.

NAME: Digital Photography
DESCRIPTION: Teaches how to use a camera and Adobe Photoshop to capture, edit, manipulate, and produce quality images for print and the Internet/Multimedia. Focuses on digital image capture and manipulation. Assessments include quizzes and hands-on exercises/projects.

NAME: Global Art & Social Impact
DESCRIPTION: Students analyze, understand, and enjoy various works of art and architecture. Main focus on modern and post-modern contemporary art. Students gain understanding of the role of arts in reflecting human thinking throughout history, build art vocabulary, and develop artistic concepts through hands-on work.

NAME: Interactive Design Level I
DESCRIPTION: Foundation course. Students work with the Arduino platform, program using Processing, and get an introduction to the Unity game engine. Foundation for more in-depth, multi-trimester projects through Interactive Design 2, 3, and Advanced Topics.

NAME: Interactive Design Level II
DESCRIPTION: Students design their own project utilizing skills acquired in Interactive Design 1. Also includes work with virtual reality and 3D printing.

NAME: Interactive Design Level III
DESCRIPTION: Students continue work on projects begun in Interactive Design 2 or propose and develop new projects.

NAME: Advanced Topics Interactive Design I
DESCRIPTION: More advanced projects combining multiple disciplines. Examples include virtual reality experiences and interactive installations.

NAME: Advanced Topics Interactive Design II
DESCRIPTION: Continuing work from Advanced Topics in Interactive Design 1. Students may also propose and develop new projects.
PREREQS: Interactive Design 1, 2, 3, and Advanced Topics Interactive Design 1

NAME: Advanced Topics Interactive Design III
DESCRIPTION: Continuing work from Advanced Topics in Interactive Design 2. Students may also propose and develop new projects.
PREREQS: Interactive Design 1, 2, 3, Advanced Topics Interactive Design 1 and 2

NAME: Intro to Photoshop
DESCRIPTION: Introductory course on how to edit and create amazing images and effects with Photoshop. Step-by-step exercises ranging from beginner to advanced techniques. Also helps prepare students for the Adobe Certified Associate (ACA) exam.

NAME: Intro to UX Design
DESCRIPTION: Students learn tools and techniques to design useful, functional, and pleasurable products. Equal focus on theoretical frameworks and practical applications, progressing through a final project to serve as an eventual portfolio piece.

NAME: Paper Art
DESCRIPTION: Various types of paper projects using different kinds of papers. Techniques include paper folding, pop-up, paper cutting, paper sculpture, and collage. Students are introduced to design concepts, aesthetics, function, technical skills, and social, cultural, and historical influences on design.

NAME: Video Production (Intro, Intermediate, Advanced)
DESCRIPTION: Intro: Students learn video production process from Pre-Production to Post-Production, including basics of non-linear editing using Adobe Premiere Pro. Intermediate: Students expand skills through production of a video project from scratch. Advanced: Students develop longer-form independent or school videos and have the opportunity to work with Adobe After Effects.
PREREQS: Intermediate and Advanced require prior completion of lower levels

NAME: Espanol I-II Accelerated
DESCRIPTION: Designed for 9th graders studying the language for the first time or with some exposure. Accelerated course meeting more often than level II. Covers essential grammar, vocabulary, and cultural material at novice level. Students create and perform original dialogues, question and answer scenarios, and various pair and group projects.

NAME: Espanol II
DESCRIPTION: Advances students' communicative abilities to the novice-high level. Topics: summer vacations, current events, past actions, biographies of Spanish-speaking celebrities, places in Spanish speaking countries, and changes over time. Goal: Novice-High proficiency.

NAME: Espanol III
DESCRIPTION: Advances students' communicative abilities to the intermediate-mid level. Topics: describing people/situations/relationships, future of environment and technology, personal future, short stories, and commands for giving advice.

NAME: Francais I-II Accelerated
DESCRIPTION: Designed for freshmen studying French for the first time or with some exposure. Covers essential grammar, vocabulary, and cultural material at novice level. Activities include creation and performance of original dialogs and skits, question and answer scenarios, and pair and group projects.

NAME: Francais II
DESCRIPTION: Advances students' communicative abilities to the novice-high level. Topics include describing oneself and others, daily life, and marketplace and restaurant interactions.

NAME: Francais III
DESCRIPTION: Advances students' communicative abilities to the intermediate-mid level. Topics include leisure activities, summer vacation, how life used to be, social conflict, and authentic literary works.

NAME: IB Espanol IV HL
DESCRIPTION: Part one of a two-year course sequence. Students use the range and complexity of the language to communicate. Develops vocabulary, grammar, and conceptual understanding of how the language works. Students summarize chapter books and use strategies to maintain flow of conversations and discussions.

NAME: IB Espanol IV SL
DESCRIPTION: Part one of a two-year course sequence. Students develop ability to communicate in Spanish at the intermediate-high skill level. Covers grammar, diversity and wellbeing, narration of the past, expressions of possibility, traditions, and social changes.

NAME: IB Espanol V HL
DESCRIPTION: Part two of the two-year course sequence. Students continue to develop knowledge of vocabulary, grammar, and conceptual understanding of how the language works in order to construct, analyze, and evaluate arguments.

NAME: IB Espanol V SL
DESCRIPTION: Part two of the two-year course sequence. Students further develop ability to communicate in Spanish at the intermediate-advanced skill level. Topics include Identities, Experiences, Sharing the Planet, Human Ingenuity, and Social Organization. Prepares students for IB exams.

NAME: IB Francais IV HL
DESCRIPTION: Part one of a two-year course sequence. Students extend range and complexity of the language to communicate at an advanced level. Emphasizes ability to analyze and develop arguments on a wide variety of topics. Students read authentic articles and literary works in light of five IB themes: identities, experiences, human ingenuity, social organization, and sharing the planet.

NAME: IB Francais IV SL
DESCRIPTION: Part one of a two-year course sequence. Language acquisition at intermediate-high linguistic level. Aims to foster appreciation and understanding of French and Francophone cultures. Five thematic units: Identities, Experiences, Human Ingenuity, Social Organization, and Sharing the Planet.

NAME: IB Francais V HL
DESCRIPTION: Part two of the two-year course sequence. Students extend range and complexity of the language to communicate at an advanced level. Continues literary exploration begun with 'Le Petit Prince,' delving into a second full-length work, typically 'Antigone' by Jean Anouilh.

NAME: IB Francais V SL
DESCRIPTION: Part two of the two-year course sequence. Language acquisition at intermediate-high linguistic level. Includes Internal Oral Assessment and externally moderated IB papers. Five thematic units: Identities, Experiences, Human Ingenuity, Social Organization, and Sharing the Planet.

NAME: IB Mandarin IV Ab Initio (SL)
DESCRIPTION: Part one of a two-year course sequence. Students reinforce knowledge of vocabulary and grammar and extend it by understanding the why and how of language: audience, context, purpose, meaning. Students expand range of communication skills by understanding and producing a wide variety of oral and written texts.

NAME: IB Mandarin V Ab Initio (SL)
DESCRIPTION: Part two of the two-year course sequence. Students develop the ability to communicate in Mandarin Chinese through study of language, themes, and texts. Careful attention to forms, structures, functions, and conceptual understandings of language.

NAME: Mandarin I-II Accelerated
DESCRIPTION: Designed for 9th graders studying Mandarin for the first time or with limited exposure. Accelerated course meeting more often than Mandarin II. Covers essential grammar, vocabulary, and cultural material at novice level. Topics include introductions, family, preferences, and simple scheduling. Students learn to read and write around 200 basic characters.

NAME: Mandarin II
DESCRIPTION: Students develop Mandarin Chinese language skills to make basic conversations on topics such as routines and daily life, rooms and furniture, clothing, food and health, weather, and entertainment. Goal: Novice Mid or Novice High proficiency per ACTFL guidelines.

NAME: Mandarin III
DESCRIPTION: Advances students' communicative abilities to the intermediate-low level through interpretive, interpersonal, and presentational activities. Topics: clothing, weather, and transportation. Students can recognize 700-1000 characters and read simple texts.

NAME: Contemporary Caribbean Art
DESCRIPTION: Introduces students to Latino artists from Mexico and the Caribbean including Cundo Bermúdez, Wifredo Lam, David Alfaro Siqueiros, Frida Kahlo, José Clemente Orozco, and Jean-Michel Basquiat. Students explore their lives and times and understand how these artists have expressed influences of pop culture, religion, politics, human suffering, and pain.

NAME: Intro to Latin Music
DESCRIPTION: Gateway for students who love music and are curious about the Spanish speaking world. Students learn about the history of music in different Spanish speaking countries and are exposed to authentic Latin music, its cultural impact, a variety of Latin music genres, musical instruments, and famous songwriters and singers.

NAME: Intro to ASL
DESCRIPTION: Four sections (A, B, C, D) using the web-based course Lifeprint. Students practice language through interviews, skits, and presentations. Section A: talking about self and family. Section B: school, home, city, and interpersonal conflicts. Section C: transportation, media, colors, and time. Section D: food, clothes, and household life. Does not count towards GPA.

NAME: Spanish Customs & Traditions
DESCRIPTION: Explores the customs and traditions of the Spanish-speaking world, including European and Indigenous customs and traditions that fused to create Latin American culture, and the influence from traditions brought by Africans to the continent during colonial times.

NAME: Veganism
DESCRIPTION: Students explore how the practice of veganism intersects with topics such as animal rights, environmentalism, health, culinary arts, social justice, feminism, psychology, and mindfulness. Students do not need to be vegan/vegetarian to enroll.

NAME: Vibrant Flavors of the Latin Cuisine
DESCRIPTION: Students research (and sample) the gastronomy in Latin America, its ingredients, history, fun facts, and some Spanish lingo that will help while ordering food.

NAME: Vibrant Flavors of the Spanish Cuisine
DESCRIPTION: Students research (and sample) the gastronomy in Spain, its ingredients, history, fun facts, and some Spanish lingo that will help while ordering food.
